pages.description: Captain Dewi Lake says he always believed Wales could defeat New Zealand and end the 73-year hoodoo against the All Blacks.
pages.text: Wales 35-28 New Zealand: Captain Dewi Lake believed in All Blacks history - BBC Sport Image source, Huw Evans Picture Agency Image caption, Dewi Lake and Jac Morgan were the Wales co-captains at the 2023 World Cup in France By Gareth Griffiths BBC Sport Wales Published 14 November 2026 Captain Dewi Lake says he always believed Wales could defeat New Zealand and end the 73-year hoodoo against the All Blacks. Wales never trailed in the 35-28 victory as they produced a magnificent display to beat New Zealand for the first time since 1953. Wales had lost the previous 34 matches in the fixture and had odds of 20-1 with the bookmakers before this game. But Lake says the group thought they could win against a New Zealand team ranked second in the world and would have gone top if they had beaten Wales. "Of course we did," said Lake. "Sometimes we sit in front of the media and say we can beat them and it's probably a passing comment for some media outlets or people at home. "It's not for us. We work hard, we have tough conversations, not only players, but coaches and staff. "There is much hard work that goes on for this group to grow and succeed. "For it to finally come to fruition and see it on the field makes me so proud." This is a special group - Tandy Figure caption, Highlights: Wales beat New Zealand for first time in 73 years Lake's sentiments were echoed by head coach Tandy, who said he felt emotional after the win. pages.title: Wales 35-28 New Zealand: Defensive desire a Welsh hallmark - Jamie Roberts - BBC Sport
pages.description: Former Wales centre Jamie Roberts says the heroic defensive effort to beat New Zealand for the first time since 1953 showed what it meant to be Welsh.
pages.text: Wales 35-28 New Zealand: Defensive desire a Welsh hallmark - Jamie Roberts - BBC Sport Image source, Press Association Image caption, Jamie Roberts (centre) never managed to beat New Zealand in his 94-cap Wales career By Gareth Griffiths BBC Sport Wales Published 15 November 2026 Former British and Irish Lions centre Jamie Roberts said Wales' heroic defensive effort against New Zealand in the 35-28 win showed what it meant to be Welsh. It was the first time since 1953 Wales celebrated beating the All Blacks, ending a run of 34 successive defeats in one of world rugby's historically most one-sided fixtures. On three separate occasions Wales led by 14 points, and for the first time they scored five tries against New Zealand, but ultimately it was heroic defence that denied the visitors. "That defensive set in the second half epitomised in a way what it is to be Welsh," Roberts, who won 94 caps for Wales, told BBC Radio 5 Live. "That resilience, that bravery, that kind of never-say-die attitude that made us all so proud." pages.description: As Welsh rugby fans wake up on Sunday morning the realisation will dawn on them that Wales beat New Zealand for the first time in 73 years.
pages.text: Wales 35-28 New Zealand: Reality dawns after Wales dared to dream - BBC Sport Figure caption, Highlights: Wales beat New Zealand for first time in 73 years By Gareth Griffiths BBC Sport Wales Published 15 November 2026 Did that really happen? Or was it just a dream? As Welsh rugby fans wake up on Sunday morning the realisation will dawn on them. It has happened. Wales have finally beaten the All Blacks again. For the first time in 73 years - after 34 defeats - 19 December 1953 is now joined by 14 November 2026 as a defining date in Welsh rugby history. Thousands of young kids will this morning be turning up to rugby training or matches, driven by parents who have a hint of a headache, with this magical day fresh in the memory. Steve Tandy‘s heroes will always have this moment, with inspirational captain Dewi Lake and player-of-the-match James Botham shedding tears. "Best day of my life," concluded Wales centre Eddie James. Many will concur. Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Wales were awarded the Raeburn Shield - presented to rugby's lineal champions - after the 35-28 win against New Zealand Why nobody was expecting a Wales win It was a result that sent shockwaves throughout Wales but also around the sporting world. Friends and relatives who had not been in contact for ages messaged each other to revel in or discuss the result. People reminisced that their parents or grandparents never saw this day. pages.description: Wales end a 73-year hoodoo against New Zealand with a win hailed as their greatest of all time.
pages.text: Wales 35-28 New Zealand: The magical day Wales beat the All Blacks again - BBC Sport Figure caption, Highlights: Wales beat New Zealand for first time in 73 years By Matt Lloyd BBC Sport Published 14 November 2026 One of the greatest Wales wins of all time. That is how former captain Sam Warburton described the monumental result against New Zealand in Cardiff on Saturday. At the time of the kick-off, the All Blacks were effectively the top-ranked side in the world following South Africa's tension-filled loss to France on Friday night. So no-one gave Wales a glimmer of hope - even Warburton - with some bookmakers offering odds of 30-1 during the week. The question, not of when but can Wales beat the All Blacks again has beset them since 1953. That 73-year wait has been marred by cheating, national scandal and pure sporting drama. Little wonder then that few wanted to leave the Principality Stadium long after the final whistle had sparked unprecedented scenes of utter joy, tears and relief to the strains of Yma O Hyd. The outpouring of unbridled emotion was after a losing run - stretching across 34 matches - that has hung like a millstone around the necks of generations of Wales players. Like so many former stars, Warburton tasted success with the British & Irish Lions but lost all five meetings with New Zealand even as part of one of the most successful Wales teams of all time during the Warren Gatland era. pages.description: Wales celebrate a first victory against New Zealand since 1953 with a brilliant 35-28 win to spark astonishing scenes in Cardiff.
pages.text: Wales 35-28 New Zealand: Wales beat All Blacks for first time since 1953 - BBC Sport Figure caption, Highlights: Wales beat New Zealand for first time in 73 years By Gareth Griffiths BBC Sport Wales Published 14 November 2026 Nations Championship Wales (21) 35 Tries: T Williams, Lake, Griffin, James, Rees-Zammit Cons: Costelow 5 New Zealand (21) 28 Tries: Ratima, Sititi, Fineanganofo, Lakai Cons: Mo'unga 4. Wales celebrated a first victory against New Zealand in 73 years with a brilliant performance to spark astonishing scenes in Cardiff. Steve Tandy's unfancied side lifted a nation as they broke a 34-match losing sequence against the All Blacks that stretched back to 1953. In a nine-try Nations Championship thriller at the Principality Stadium, Wales led 14-0, 21-7 and 35-21 before they held off New Zealand with a wonderful defensive display in the final quarter, led by flankers James Botham and Jac Morgan and lock Dafydd Jenkins. The home side produced a stunning start with tries from inspirational scrum-half Tomos Williams and captain Dewi Lake inside the first six minutes. Prop Archie Griffin also added a first-half try, but New Zealand responded with scores from scrum-half Cortez Ratima, number eight Wallace Sititi and wing Fehi Fineanganofo to level the score 21-21 at half-time. Wales centre Eddie James and wing Louis Rees-Zammit scored early second-half tries before New Zealand flanker Peter Lakai pulled one back. pages.description: Wales made a record amount of tackles in the win against New Zealand, with contributions from the whole squad.
pages.text: Wales beat New Zealand: Replacements show tackling prowess in Nations Championship win - BBC Sport Image source, Huw Evans Picture Agency Image caption, Ben Carter and Gareth Thomas are part of Wales' 39-man squad for the Nations Championship By Gareth Griffiths BBC Sport Wales Published 18 November 2026 They say rugby is now a game that relies on 23 players. There was ample evidence of that during Wales' remarkable 35-28 win against New Zealand last Saturday. The headline acts were the 346 tackles made by the team, which was a world record for an international match. The 38 tackles managed by lock Dafydd Jenkins matched the top individual tally, while Jac Morgan (31), James Botham (30), Eddie James (25), captain Dewi Lake (24) and Max Llewellyn (23) were not far behind. It was the impact of the bench that also proved crucial in the defensive stand of the final quarter. Replacement back rower Taine Plumtree popped up with two crucial turnovers, while Gareth Thomas and Ben Carter made a combined 32 tackles in 42 minutes. Ospreys prop Thomas managed 19 in 26 minutes, while lock Carter's return was 13 in 16 minutes to add to the remarkable statistics and contributions. pages.text: Wales v Australia: Five key areas for Steve Tandy's side to back up All Blacks win - BBC Sport Image source, Huw Evans Picture Agency Image caption, Despite beating New Zealand and Japan this November, Wales lie fifth of the six teams in the Nations Championship Northern Hemisphere table By Matt Lloyd BBC Sport Wales Published 17 November 2026 As the dust settles on Wales' historic victory over New Zealand, work is under way to secure another major scalp. Steve Tandy's side ensured their place in history by ending the 73-year wait for a win against the All Blacks. Now they must back up what many are describing as the one of the greatest results in Welsh rugby history by beating Australia in Cardiff on Saturday. Wales have won just one of their past five meetings with the Wallabies and are without a victory over them in Cardiff since 2021. But victory would complete only their second ever clean sweep of autumn internationals following the statement win on Saturday. "[Beating the All Blacks] wasn't even by fluke, that's the nicest thing," former Wales centre Tom Shanklin told the Scrum V podcast. "It wasn't like there were two or three cards for New Zealand. Wales did it the hard way and deserved to win." So what must Wales get right this week on the final weekend of the Nations Championship group stage? pages.text: Wales v Australia: Steve Tandy makes four changes to side that beat All Blacks - BBC Sport Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Aaron Wainwright and Josh Adams both missed the historic win over the All Blacks By Chris Kirwan BBC Sport Wales Published 9 hours ago Wales have made four changes to the side that made history against New Zealand for the Nations Championship fixture against Australia. Head coach Steve Tandy has tinkered with the starting line-up that beat the All Blacks for the first time in 73 years at Principality Stadium. Wales go with the same XV that opened the Nations Championship with a 28-21 victory against Japan. Alex Mann comes in for James Botham at blind-side flanker, Aaron Wainwright is back from a leg injury at number eight, lock Ben Carter returns for the injured Adam Beard and Josh Adams gets the nod on the wing. Botham was man of the match against New Zealand but is not included after a huge defensive effort. His partner is expecting their first child this week, but Wales say that is not the reason for the flanker sitting out the Wallabies game. pages.text: Wales v Australia: Steve Tandy's squad witness Wales delight but turn attention to Australia - BBC Sport Image source, Huw Evans Picture Agency Image caption, Wales won their first three games against New Zealand but have had to wait 73 years for a fourth By Gareth Griffiths BBC Sport Wales Published 17 November 2026 Wales' battered and bruised rugby heroes have been using the reaction of the nation to help soothe their aches and pains as they prepare for their next challenge. Steve Tandy's squad came back to training on Monday, 48 hours after their famous 35-28 win saw them become the first Wales side to defeat the All Blacks since 1953. Wales had celebrated the victory on Saturday night, and the squad assembled as a whole a little later on Monday than in previous weeks as attention now turns to facing Australia this Saturday in Cardiff. There was a video shown during one of the team meetings about what the All Blacks victory meant to fans. "The players came in a bit later on Monday after being given a bit of time off to enjoy the feeling with their families," said Wales assistant coach Matt Sherratt. "We kind of reviewed the New Zealand game yesterday, but let the lads enjoy it as well. "That was powerful in terms of the reaction from friends, families and the country as a whole. "The group deserved to feel that yesterday also and we showed them what it meant to the country. "The boys loved watching some of the videos we've seen, some of the memes online about people's reactions in their living rooms. That's what it's all about." Walker Lake and the Sportsman's Beach Recreation Site is located in Mineral County, Nevada. This lake is a rare perennial lake of the Great Basin and is important for a variety of resident and migratory wildlife species. Approximately 38,000 acres in size, Walker Lake is the most prominent geographical feature in the region and the primary focal point for recreation in the area. Walker Lake offers a variety of recreational opportunities including swimming, picnicking, boating, bird watching, water-skiing and camping. Sportsman's Beach provides thirty one individual camp sites plus two undeveloped camping areas that accommodate RV and tent campers. Facilities include vault toilets, covered picnic tables, grills, pull through and back-in camp sites, paved access and a public boat ramp area. That’s not surprising given that we’re all hearing about rising rates of dementia as the population ages: A study in the January issue of Nature Medicine suggested that by the year 2060, the number of adults in the U.S. who will develop dementia is likely to double to a million people. That’s a club no one wants to join. Fortunately, science is showing that healthy eating habits can have a powerful impact on protecting cognitive function and memory . pages.text: Washington's Trials, Lesson 4 | Crash Course: American Revolution | National Geographic Premium HISTORY & CULTURE CRASH COURSE Washington’s Trials Lesson 4: Defeated in New York and pursued by redcoats, a beleaguered continental army triumphed at Trenton—and revived the revolutionary cause. By the time the United States declared independence on July 4, 1776 , Washington’s army was in New York City, anticipating a British invasion. New York was home to many British loyalists, or Tories, but some had fled and others were lying low to avoid harassment by American revolutionaries. New York’s royal governor, William Tryon, had taken refuge offshore on a British sloop of war in October 1775 and plotted to assassinate Washington, a scheme exposed in June 1776 . Patriots infuriated by the plot went after suspected Tories and scourged them. One witness saw men “being carried through the streets on rails, their clothes tore from their back and their bodies pretty well mingled with the dust.” Shortly after the Declaration of Independence was read in the city, 40 colonial soldiers and sailors celebrated by hauling down a large-scale gilded lead statue of King George III on horseback at the city’s Bowling Green park, severing the head, and sending parts of the statue to Connecticut, where the metal was recast to form musket balls for Washington’s forces. Over the previous few months, every plateau, peninsula, island, and mountain ridge on Earth had been painstakingly hand-painted on the five foot diameter 100-pound sphere. Today, a final coat of watercolor paint is laid on, but then, a new challenge arises: how to get it out of the studio. The completed globe is so large that it doesn’t fit through the front door. Instead, a crane plucks the globe, now placed in a shipment crate, from the studio’s roof and sets it in the quiet alleyway, where it starts a transatlantic journey to be installed at the new National Geographic Museum of Exploration, opening this week. Much about traditional globe making hasn’t changed since the 16th century. But Bellerby & Co is a relative newcomer to the craft. In 2008, owner Peter Bellerby was working in real estate when he went searching for a handcrafted globe for his father’s 80th birthday. Video: Alex Grabham By Jack Tamisiea Published April 20, 2026 Kea parrots are known for being extremely curious and capable of solving complex problems ; they can even make each other chuckle . Now, for the first time, a kea named Bruce has demonstrated skilled combat techniques after losing his upper beak. Despite missing a facial feature thought to be crucial for survival, Bruce has worked his way to becoming the alpha male of his circus, the collective noun for a group of kea, at the Willowbank Wildlife Reserve in Christchurch, New Zealand. These olive-green parrots have fiery orange feathers under their wings and live in the mountains of New Zealand’s South Island. This Balinese family is helping the insects make a comeback—and ecotourism plays a key role. Wayan Wardika, founder of the firefly conservation project Bring Back The Light, says it takes years for populations to recover. “They are in the early stages, so this won't look like the clouds of fireflies you see in the Smokies, for example—it's gradual, not to mention a different species,” he says.
